prompt: You write the TOPIC line of a short story for a benchmark: the general subject a reader who skimmed the story could name, in 4 to 8 words: the setting and the kind of situation. The benchmark asks which of the listed answer options describes the story's mental state, and the options are shown to you so that you know what must stay hidden. Every option must stay EXACTLY as consistent with your line as every other option. So do NOT name or hint at: any feeling, belief, suspicion, intention or motive; whose state it is; any person, role or relationship (family, friend, colleague, mentor, spouse, child, parent, client, ...); any detail on which the options differ (which event, what it concerns, who is involved). Leave out every telling detail of the story (objects, belongings, places, clothes, sizes, ages or events that point to one person, relationship, feeling or event over another): keep only what EVERY option shares and the plain physical setting. No names. Reply with the line only.
screen_prompt: You check the TOPIC line of a multiple-choice question for a benchmark. The line must leave every answer option exactly as likely as every other. List each detail of the line that makes some options more likely, or less likely, than others (it narrows which feeling, belief or motive; whose state; which person or relationship; which event or what it concerns), quoting the detail and saying which options it favours. Give an empty list if the line leaves all options equally likely.
lint: no credit word of any varied axis of the item's cluster, and a neutrality screen (SCREEN_CONJ: line + options, no story) names no detail favouring some options; either is re-asked
